title: 'Gender apartheid': How the Taliban have trampled women's rights for five years
subhead: 'Voices of Afghan Women' (2/6). Upon returning to power on August 15, 2021, the Taliban dismantled institutions, laws and services related to women's rights in a matter of days and purged the judicial system of all female presence. Here is the next installment of testimonies collected by our reporter in Kabul.

title: From Napoleon's camels to D-Day's dogs: The animals drafted into war
subhead: 'Animal Soldiers' (1/6). Le Monde recounts the forgotten animals who served on battlefields, such as Glen the dog and his master Emile. Killed together in Normandy on June 6, 1944, they were buried side by side in the Ranville military cemetery.

Mahmoud Darwish and Tamar Ben Ami: The impossible love of a Palestinian poet and an Israeli dancer
subhead: In the early 1960s, in Haifa, Israel, the young Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish fell in love with Tamar Ben Ami, a Jewish Israeli dancer. Their romance was intense but brief. From this forbidden love, the writer composed a poignant poem, 'Rita and the Rifle,' which is still sung throughout the Arab world.

title: Environmental amnesia: How we can't even remember the lost biodiversity of yore
subhead: While we can recall car windshields covered with dead insects after a drive, what do we know about wolves that once roamed the countryside in the Middle Ages, or salmon swimming in the Seine in the 19th century? This gradual forgetting of what was once a teeming natural world prevents us from protecting today's nature.

title: Tiananmen Square massacre: Le Monde reveals unseen footage of the Chinese regime's violent repression
subhead: Art historian Nathalie Trouveroy shared footage with Le Monde from her personal archives of the Tiananmen Square protests, shedding new light on how the Chinese regime violently repressed the student protests in June 1989.
